Authenticity.title: Is your SKF bearing genuine?
Authenticity.subtitle: Counterfeit bearings look convincing and fail early. Here is how to check a bearing you already have, and how to avoid the problem altogether.

risk.p: Counterfeiters buy cheap ISO-standard bearings and add fake SKF markings and boxes. To an untrained eye they look identical, but nobody knows whether they meet the load, safety or service-life requirements of your machine. A failed bearing means unplanned downtime at best, and damaged gears, shafts and housings at worst.

stats.label: of counterfeit bearings destroyed by SKF together with law enforcement in 2017
fake items in that single seizure, headed for ordinary supply chains
Up to half of company managers may have bought counterfeit parts without knowing

source.h: The surest check: buy from an authorised distributor
source.p: B&B Unikoop is the official SKF distributor for North Macedonia. Every bearing we sell comes straight from SKF's supply chain, so there is nothing to verify.

app.h: Check a bearing with SKF Authenticate
app.p: Bought SKF products elsewhere and have doubts? SKF's free app sends your photos directly to SKF experts, who reply by email.

photos.p: Take 5–10 sharp photos of the box and the bearing from every side. The more detail, the better.

items: Install SKF Authenticate from the App Store or Google Play.
Open the app, tap Start and choose “Use existing photos” (or take new ones). Select your photos and tap Next.
Enter who you bought the product from, a short comment such as “Please check whether this SKF product is genuine”, and your contact details. SKF replies to that email address, so double-check it.
Tap Send and confirm. You get an automatic receipt right away, and SKF's verdict within a few hours to a few days.

Authenticity.more: Unsure about a bearing you already have? <contact>Send us photos</contact> and our technical service will help, or read more about <skf>SKF brand protection</skf>.

housings: SNL/SNH split plummer block housings in series 2, 3, 5 and 6, built on a modular principle.
Split horizontally into cap and base, so the bearing can be inspected or replaced without taking the shaft out.
SNH housings in grey cast iron GG 20; heavy-duty SSNHD housings in spheroidal graphite cast iron. Dimensions to ISO 113/II.
Seal options: double-lip (TG), V-ring (TA), felt (TC) and special labyrinth sets.
Supports free or locating bearing arrangements (locating rings fitted as needed).
sleeves: Adapter and withdrawal sleeves for mounting tapered-bore bearings on cylindrical shafts.
All standard dimensions and series; adapter sleeves come complete with lock nut and locking device.
Adapter sleeves have a 1:12 outer taper and black-oxide finish; OH…H versions support the oil-injection method.
Withdrawal sleeves for 1:12 and 1:30 tapers (240 K30 and 241 K30 series); suffix G means a smaller thread.
speedi-sleeve: Thin-walled 0.28 mm wear sleeve pushed over the worn shaft — no disassembly or shaft machining.
A seal of the same size as the original can be used.
The installation tool comes with each sleeve; a hammer is all you need.
Standard range for shaft diameters from 11.99 to 203.33 mm (0.472–8 in); other sizes on request.
shim-packs: Pre-cut single-slot shims for accurate vertical machine alignment.
Five dimensions and ten thicknesses, plus kits with the most popular combinations.
High-quality stainless steel — reusable, easy to fit and remove, with close tolerances.
The thickness is clearly marked on every shim.
vibracon: Self-levelling adjustable chocks for mounting rotating equipment on base frames or steel and concrete foundations.
Accept up to 4° of angle between machine and foundation without machining the foundation.
Eliminate soft foot; high load capacity and a wide adjustment range with a low profile.
Typical machines: gas and diesel engines, compressors, electric motors, gearboxes, generators, pumps, fans and turbines.
Used in food and beverage, pulp and paper, oil and gas, marine and offshore, railways and power generation.
y-bearings: Deep groove ball bearings, greased and sealed on both sides, with a sphered outer ring that accepts initial misalignment.
Locked to the shaft by eccentric collar or grub screws (YAR, YAJ, YET series); adapter-sleeve and inch versions available.
Lithium-based grease as standard; glass-fibre reinforced polyamide 6,6 cages up to +110 °C.
Y-bearing units in cast iron, zinc-coated pressed steel or composite housings: pillow block, flanged and take-up.
composite-housing-units: Housings in glass-fibre reinforced polyamide (PA6): light and resistant to corrosion, chemicals and diluted acids.
Tolerate high and low temperatures, UV resistant and recyclable; end caps available.
Bearings are greased for life with water-resistant grease — no relubrication needed.
ISO pillow block, square and oval flanged units, with any SKF insert bearing of matching size.
seals: Radial shaft seals, V-rings and hydraulic seals, including CR Seals — founded in 1878 as Chicago Rawhide and part of SKF since 1990.
Lip materials with high chemical and thermal resistance, robust design, built to national and international standards.
Typical applications: gearboxes, hydraulic pumps, axles, power-steering columns, speed reducers and transmissions.
Also HMS5 and HMSA10 radial shaft seals and SKF Taconite seals for heavily contaminated conditions.
cooper: Split roller bearing invented by Thomas Cooper in 1907; Cooper is an SKF company.
Split to the shaft, so it fits without removing couplings, gears or neighbouring bearings — far shorter downtime.
Clearances are preset: no on-site adjustment or special tools needed.
Ideal for hard-to-reach positions and long shafts supported at several points.
Units offer lifting screws, inspection holes and tapped holes for temperature and vibration sensors.
